(November 23, 2026) – Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: KYMR), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing a new class of oral small molecule degrader medicines for immunological diseases, today announced positive 16-week results from the BROADEN2 Phase 2b trial of KT-621, its first-in-class, once-daily oral STAT6 degrader, in patients with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The trial met its primary endpoint of percent change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score at Week 16 and secondary endpoints, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo across all dose cohorts. The BROADEN2 findings support advancement of KT-621 into late-stage development, with the first Phase 3 AD trial planned to initiate by mid-2027, subject to alignment with regulators, as well as potential expansion in other Type 2 indications. “Today’s results mark a pivotal moment in the field of immunology, demonstrating what truly groundbreaking science can achieve in areas of significant patient need. The BROADEN2 results exceeded our expectations, reinforcing our belief that KT-621 represents one of the largest opportunities in biopharma, with the potential to transform care for millions of people living with Type 2 inflammatory diseases,” said Nello Mainolfi, PhD, Founder, President and CEO, Kymera Therapeutics. “What stands out is the combination of improvements in disease severity and itch beginning as early as Week 1, significant continued responses across all dose cohorts at Week 16, and a favorable safety profile. The overall clinical activity supports the potential to deliver the level of disease control historically reported with approved biologics such as dupilumab. The mid dose, which we selected to achieve optimal STAT6 pharmacology, consistently delivered the largest numerical improvements across endpoints and is well positioned to advance towards Phase 3.” Dr. Mainolfi continued, “These findings strengthen our conviction that KT-621 could substantially expand the number of patients receiving an advanced therapy. By overcoming the longstanding scientific challenge of directly targeting STAT6, we have taken a clear step toward our vision of delivering the first oral therapy for the full spectrum of Type 2 diseases, beginning in AD. Additionally, these results validate the scientific expertise and translational capabilities behind our innovation engine and our approach of pairing the right targets with the right technology to create a new era of oral medicines. As we advance KT-621 toward Phase 3, we are building an expanding franchise with the potential to reshape care across immunology. Importantly, we thank the patients and their families for their trust and commitment, and the investigators and study teams for their dedication to advancing this unique new treatment for AD.” “In my practice, I see many patients living with AD who continue to struggle with persistent symptoms and the daily burden of managing this chronic condition,” said Eric Simpson, MD, MCR, lead investigator on the BROADEN2 study and Frances J. Storrs Medical Dermatology Professor and Director of CLEAR Eczema Center, Oregon Health & Science University. “A targeted oral therapy that combines robust clinical activity with favorable safety and tolerability could expand the number of patients receiving systemic treatment and help them achieve and maintain disease control. KT-621 brings an innovative mechanism to a well-established pathway in Type 2 inflammation by targeting STAT6. The highly encouraging BROADEN2 findings suggest a compelling profile and reinforce the potential of this program to address the substantial unmet need in AD.” BROADEN2 Phase 2b Trial Design and Baseline Characteristics BROADEN2 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, dose-ranging trial evaluating the clinical activity, safety and tolerability of KT-621 in 244 adult and adolescent patients with moderate to severe AD. Patients were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive a low dose (n=61), mid dose (n=61) or high dose (n=63) of KT-621, or placebo (n=59), once daily for 16 weeks. Patients completing 16 weeks of treatment were eligible to participate in a 52-week open-label extension following the treatment period. Baseline characteristics were generally balanced across the four treatment groups. The mean baseline EASI score was approximately 28, and the mean baseline Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PPNRS) score was 7.1. Patients with severe disease based on a validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) score of 4 represented 38% of the study population, and 33% of patients had received prior biologic therapy. Of the 244 randomized patients, 234 completed the 16-week double-blind treatment period, and 230 of those patients enrolled in the open-label extension. (AP Photo/Haven Daley, File) · Associated Press · AP Photo/Haven Daley The Associated Press Mon, November 23, 2026 at 5:05 AM PST 2 min read CRWD -8.23% ZS +18.66% CrowdStrike is buying cloud security company Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion, the companies said Monday, in a major acquisition that combines two of the cybersecurity industry's biggest names. The all-stock deal arrives after a string of high-profile hacks hit banks, supermarket fridges and crypto platforms, forcing the White House to shake up its cybersecurity leadership and raising alarms with officials around the world. Cybersecurity experts have warned that artificial intelligence is being used to turbocharge cyberattacks by making it quicker and easier to find software flaws. "Security used to be about keeping the adversary out," George Kurtz, CEO of Austin, Texas-based Crowdstrike, said in a statement. "Today, safety is required to let AI in." Reports of advanced artificial intelligence models deploying agents working on their own to break into other organizations have also raised alarms. "In the AI era, Zero Trust security has become non-negotiable, and AI agents are rapidly becoming the new weakest link," Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry said. Crowdstrike's focus has been on so-called endpoint security, with services to protect laptops, mobile devices and desktop computers. Santa Clara, California-based Zscaler, meanwhile, specializes in cloud-based network protection. Zscaler shareholders will get 1.135 shares of Crowdstrike for each Zscaler share they own, under the deal's terms, which represent a 34% premium to Zscaler's closing price on Friday. Shares of CrowdStrike tumbled more than 7% before the opening bell Monday. Shares of Zscaler rose 20%. Existing CrowdStrike shareholders will own about 84.1% of the combined company, while existing Zscaler shareholders will hold the remaining 15.9%. CrowdStrike and Zscaler were already working together in a partnership that included 2,000 shared customers. The deal would expand the combined company's market by more than $185 billion by 2029. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of Crowdstrike's fiscal 2028 year, which begins in February. ET SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 — Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for rare diseases, today announced that it received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the U.S.

filings.text: EX-99.1 2 capr-ex99d1.htm EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Capricor Therapeutics Provides Regulatory Update on Deramiocel BLA for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy ● Company receives Complete Response Letter from FDA for Deramiocel BLA ● Conference call and webcast Monday, November 23, at 8:30 a.m. ET SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 — Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for rare diseases, today announced that it received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its resubmitted Biologics License Application (BLA) for Deramiocel, its investigational cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies. “We are deeply disappointed for the boys and young men living with Duchenne and their families,” said Linda Marbán, Ph.D., Capricor’s Chief Executive Officer. “Deramiocel has been studied in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, HOPE-2 and HOPE-3, both of which met their primary endpoints. We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval. We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.” As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of approximately $198.5 million, which it believes is sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months. The Company is reviewing its operating costs to further extend its cash runway. To participate via a webcast, please click here. A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the conclusion of the live event and will be accessible in the Investors section of the Company’s website. About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited. About Deramiocel Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, evaluated in clinical studies for its potential to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. Users, applications, and now AI agents connect directly to the cloud, and that traffic never comes back through the data center. Firewalls and VPNs built to guard the data center can’t see, inspect, or stop that traffic, the threats coming in, or the data going out. Zscaler’s SSE is purpose-built for the AI era, with the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange sitting inline between every user, agent, and application to enforce zero trust on every connection.
